metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Bulgaria

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Bulgaria using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The excerpt does not specify whether student/sampling weights or replicate weights were applied in the production of the reported means, percentages, and differences, nor does it name any weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate design (e.g., BRR/jackknife). For PISA analyses, analysts should use the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights provided in the database when estimating standard errors and confidence intervals, especially because students are sampled within schools and countries. Because this is a descriptive results factsheet rather than an ML modeling paper, the appropriate weighting guidance is to follow the PISA technical documentation for complex survey design; the present text does not provide enough detail to confirm whether weights were applied in the factsheet computations.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because the provided factsheet excerpt reports scaled creative thinking proficiency scores and descriptive comparisons/associations rather than documenting an explicit PV-based estimation procedure for a student-level predictive model. The excerpt also does not describe any missing-data strategy (e.g., how item nonresponse or questionnaire missingness was handled) because it is a results factsheet summarizing OECD outputs rather than a methodological paper detailing imputation or deletion rules. This is therefore a reporting gap for missing-data handling details in the excerpt, not necessarily a gap in the underlying OECD PISA production pipeline.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample reported for Bulgaria consists of 6,107 students in 202 schools who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 53,400 15-year-olds. The factsheet does not further specify additional filtering (e.g., grade restrictions beyond the PISA target age of 15-year-olds, exclusions for missing background variables, or any creative-thinking-specific completion criteria) in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Bulgaria’s performance on the PISA Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment includes 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Bulgaria’s mean creative thinking score is 21 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average of 33. The factsheet also reports proficiency distribution benchmarks: 39% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline), and 8% are top performers at Levels 5–6. It further describes within-country performance gaps by socio-economic status (14.2 score-point advantage for top quartile vs bottom quartile) and gender (girls +3.2 points), and highlights that creative thinking is positively associated with mathematics and reading performance, while relative strengths differ by ideation process and domain context. The excerpt does not provide the underlying technical details on weighting, PV estimation, or missing-data handling used to generate these OECD estimates.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is an OECD PISA results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. As such, it does not report an ML modeling pipeline (no algorithms, no predictive targets, no model metrics) and therefore main_findings and confounders_identified are intentionally empty. The excerpt also provides limited methodological detail on survey weighting and missing-data procedures, which are typically specified in the main PISA technical documentation rather than in a country factsheet.
